Hi Elisabeth,

Thanks for the clear summary and for attaching the draft. Short answer: we can support a split invoice + reverse-charge treatment for the venue line provided we can validate Heimathalles German VAT ID and get the required commercial evidence.

Two options we typically offer:
1) Split invoice approach (preferred): Redwood issues two invoice lines (organizer services -> EventWorks UK; venue pass-through -> Heimathalle DE). If Heimathalle supplies a valid DE VAT ID, we can apply reverse-charge on the line billed to them (no German VAT charged). This requires: VAT ID for Heimathalle, a contractual or booking confirmation showing Heimathalle is the recipient of that supply, and a PO/reference if available.

2) Single-invoice/charge-now: If we dont have validated VAT evidence before billing, we must charge German VAT at the applicable rate (19%). If Heimathalle later provides a valid VAT ID and evidence, we can issue a credit/revised invoice and refund the VAT amount.

Ive looped in Marissa (tax) and Ben (finance ops) to confirm the exact evidence list and turnaround. If youre able to send Heimathalles VAT ID and a quick scan of the venue booking confirmation, we can get the revised invoice to you same day.

Best,

Hi all,

Thanks for looping me in. Quick tax note and the evidence checklist attached. Key points for EU cross-border supply of services where the recipient is a business (B2B):

- Place of supply: For services directly supplied to a business established in another EU member state, place of supply is generally the customers location (DE for Heimathalle). Reverse-charge (Article 196) typically applies when the recipient is VAT-registered and the supplier is not required to charge local VAT.

- Evidence required before applying reverse-charge at billing time:
  * Valid VAT registration number for Heimathalle (format DE#########). We will validate on the VIES registry.
  * A copy of the venue booking confirmation showing Heimathalle as the entity receiving the service, with dates and reference.
  * A commercial contract or invoice routing instruction from EventWorks confirming the pass-through arrangement.
  * Payment instructions (bank details) for Heimathalle if Redwood is to remit on their behalf.

- If evidence is not validated at billing: we must charge German VAT (19%) on the venue line. If you provide valid evidence post-billing, Redwood can issue a corrected invoice and refund/credit the VAT amount; refunds follow our finance refund SLA (typically 7-10 business days after validation).

- Special note on documentation: keep the VIES validation screenshot and the booking confirmation; tax audits commonly request those. Our attached checklist (vat-evidence-checklist.xlsx) outlines the minimum fields we need.

Ill validate the VAT ID once you send it and confirm whether we can proceed with reverse-charge before your remittance window.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Tax & Treasury Manager, Redwood Inference
